rules.assertion: Genre, shelf, and list names use Title Case, allowing lowercase short connectives.
match_examples: Top 10 Movies on Netflix Right Now
rules.note: Every genre-name, shelf-heading, and list-name occurrence is in the denominator.

rules.assertion: When a recognized content-unit token appears, it closes the name.
counter_examples: Top 10 Movies on Netflix Right Now
Top 10 Movies on Netflix Right Now
rules.note: Counter-examples include Top 10 sentence frames and facet labels, where a locale, time, or platform clause follows the unit.

rules.assertion: Audience, origin, tone, era, brand, curation, and temporal modifiers precede the final content unit.
counter_examples: Top 10 Movies on Netflix Right Now
Top 10 Movies on Netflix Right Now
rules.note: Eligible names contain at least one lexicon-matched modifier and one recognized content unit.

rules.assertion: The initialism TV is always rendered in all caps.
rules.note: The denominator is every naming item containing TV in any casing.

rules.assertion: Top 10 selector labels use content unit, a vertical bar, then language: [Movies|Shows] | [English|Non-English].
rules.note: The denominator is every naming item containing a vertical bar.

rules.assertion: Names with a coordinating connective use & rather than the word and.
counter_examples: Drug Lords, Mob Bosses, and Gangsters
Drug Lords, Mob Bosses, and Gangsters
Drug Lords, Mob Bosses, and Gangsters
rules.note: A name containing both forms would count as a counter-example; none is silently removed.

terminology.scope: Exact whole-term occurrences in genre-name, shelf-heading, and list-name items; UI labels and title names are excluded.
terminology.verdict: The public product naming corpus uses the movie/show family 691 times (Movies + TV Shows + bare Shows) versus 32 uses of Series + Films.

derived_records.concept: the content-unit family used in Netflix's public product taxonomy, shelves, and Top 10 list names
derived_records.assertion: Public product names use the movie/show family 691 times versus 32 uses of the series/film family in this crawl; this record proposes movie/show as the product-register extension.

evidence.confidence_note: Counts are exact whole-term matches across every naming item in the signed-out crawl; repeated headings on different source URLs remain separate occurrences.

derived_records.machine_route: variant-flagging, not yet active: if adopted for this register, flag Series or Films where a product taxonomy/list content unit is intended; do not apply to editorial prose.
derived_records.localization_note: These are public product taxonomy labels, so locale-specific translations should preserve the content-type distinction while allowing the target language's normal number and compounding.

derived_records.concept: casing of public genre, shelf, and list names
derived_records.assertion: 1281 of 1297 public naming occurrences use Title Case; 16 counter-examples are retained rather than normalized away.

evidence.confidence_note: The denominator is the complete naming corpus; UI labels and title names are excluded before casing is tested.

derived_records.machine_route: casing check, not yet active: if adopted, flag non-Title-Case genre, shelf, or list names for review rather than auto-fixing the observed hyphenated counter-examples.
derived_records.localization_note: Title Case is English-specific and should not be exported as a locale-independent capitalization rule.

derived_records.concept: casing of the TV initialism in public product names
derived_records.assertion: All 196 naming items containing the initialism render it as TV; no Tv or tv counter-example was observed.

evidence.confidence_note: The casing check scans every naming item case-insensitively, then tests the original matched form.

derived_records.machine_route: exact-match casing check, not yet active: if adopted, flag Tv or tv in this public product naming register.
derived_records.localization_note: The Latin-script initialism may remain TV in many locales, but a locale owner should decide whether transliteration or a local term takes precedence.

derived_records.concept: coordinating connective in public genre and shelf names
derived_records.assertion: Of 70 public naming occurrences with a coordinating connective, 66 use & and 4 use and.

evidence.confidence_note: Every name containing either connective is counted; names with both would be counter-examples.

derived_records.machine_route: connective review, not yet active: if adopted, flag and in short public genre/shelf names while retaining a human exception path.
derived_records.localization_note: The preference is English-surface punctuation, not a universal localization rule; translated conjunctions must follow locale norms.
